Statements: Some deposits are bonds. All bonds are lockers. No lockers is a accounts.
Conclusions:
I. Some deposits are lockers.
II. Some bonds are accounts.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:
I. Some deposits are not bonds.
II. No bonds is a accounts.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:

I. All deposits are accounts.
II. No bonds is a accounts.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
rural secure credit = to pa su
rural access savings = pa ni vo
secure access banking = to vo re
credit savings banking = su ni re
rural secure banking = re to pa
What is the code for “credit”?
questions.explanation: Answer: su. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: rural = pa, secure = to, credit = su, access = vo, savings = ni, banking = re.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 67 km east, turns left and walks 72 km, then turns left and walks 13 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 90. Net displacement is 54 km east and 72 km north. By Pythagoras, √(54² + 72²) = 90 km.

questions.stem: A is the mother of H. D is the daughter of H. C is the father of H. How is D related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. C is a parent of H, and D is H’s daughter. Hence D is C’s grandchild.

questions.stem: E is the brother of H. H is the mother of D. B is the father of E and H. How is E related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. E is the brother of D’s mother H. Therefore E is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: D is the only daughter of G. G is the father of D. C is the son of D. E is the sister of G. How is G related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. G is the father of D, and D is C’s mother. Thus G is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 44 candidates, a candidate is 8th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 34. New front rank = 8+3 = 11. Back rank = 44 − 11 + 1 = 34.

questions.stem: In a queue of 55 candidates, a candidate is 13th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 39. New front rank = 13+4 = 17. Back rank = 55 − 17 + 1 = 39.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2800 each. One earns 25% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 5351.11. Recover each cost separately: 2800×100/125 + 2800×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 22 and 33 hours. An outlet empties it in 33 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank.
questions.explanation: Answer: 22. Net rate = 1/22 + 1/33 − 1/33 = 1/22. Take the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A boat covers 96 km in still water in 8 hours. If the stream flows at 2 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 4 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 40. Still-water speed = 12 km/h. Upstream speed = 12 − 2. Distance = speed × 4.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 8:3. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 3 months. A receives ₹163200 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 178500. Profit ratio is 96:9. Each ratio unit = ₹1700. Total = 105 × 1700.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹19000 earns ₹2850 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 20947.5. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 5%. Compound amount = 19000 × (1 + 5/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 100 litres of pure milk. 20 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain?
questions.explanation: Answer: 64. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 100 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 29 people is 25 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 55. New total minus old total = (29+1)×(25+1) − 29×25 = 55.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 10 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+10)/(x+10) = 3/2 gives x = 10. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 230 m train moving at 100.8 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 14.4 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 9.58. Relative speed = (100.8 − 14.4) ×5/18 = 24 m/s. Time = 230/24.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 50%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹3400. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 33.33. New quantity / old quantity = 100/150. Reduction percentage = 50/150 ×100.
